- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early/medium horizon (first 10–15 days of forecast).
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-90+ values), often overshooting by 5–10%.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing downward trends; delays mean reversion by 3–5 days.
- Tends to overcorrect upward momentum, creating artificial peaks that don’t materialize.
- Mean reversion is too aggressive — model prematurely assumes prices will return to historical mean, ignoring volatility persistence.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <80), leading to overly conservative forecasts.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days, suggesting poor initialization or lagged signal processing.
